sub: Named after “the morning brightness” (aḍ-ḍuḥā), its first word
theme: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ when revelation paused: Allah has not left him, what is coming is better, and He has cared for him since birth. So care for the orphan and the asker, and speak of Allah’s blessings.
story: Revealed early in Makkah. For a time, Jibrīl stopped coming and revelation paused. The Prophet ﷺ was deeply saddened.

The idolaters mocked: “His Lord has abandoned him and hates him.” Reportedly a woman, said to be Umm Jamīl, the wife of Abū Lahab, taunted him after he was ill and missed night prayer for two or three nights.

The surah answered them. When Jibrīl returned, the Prophet ﷺ told him he had longed for him. Reportedly he said “Allāhu akbar” for joy, and in the Makkan reading reciters say it between surahs from here to the end.

sections.title: Your Lord has not left you
sections.meaning: By the bright morning and the still night: your Lord has not abandoned you, and He is not displeased with you. What comes later is better for you than what came first, and your Lord will give you until you are pleased.
points: By the morning light and the still night
Your Lord has not left you or hated you
What comes later is better than what came first
Your Lord will give you until you are pleased
sections.matters: It answers a painful taunt with two denials and two promises. Like the quiet of night after a bright day, a pause is part of Allah’s plan, not a sign that He has turned away.
sections.story: Revelation paused, reportedly for somewhere between twelve and forty days. The idolaters said, “Muhammad’s Lord has abandoned him and hates him.” These ayat were the reply.
explained: Allah swears by aḍ-ḍuḥā, the morning light, and by the night when sajā: it settles and grows still. Mā waddaʿaka: your Lord has not said goodbye to you since He chose you, wa mā qalā: nor has He hated you since He loved you.

Al-ākhirah is better than al-ūlā: the Hereafter is better than this world, and each later stage of his life would be better than the one before. And your Lord will give you until you are pleased: victory and Islam spreading here, and intercession for his ummah there.
teaches: A pause in blessing is not a sign Allah is displeased.
What is coming can be better than what has passed.
Allah’s giving goes on until you are satisfied.
sections.hook: Two denials (mā waddaʿaka, mā qalā), then two promises that both start wa la-: wa la-l-ākhiratu (4) and wa la-sawfa (5). Ayah 5 ends fa-tarḍā.

sections.title: Remember His care, then care for others
sections.meaning: Allah reminds him: you were an orphan and He sheltered you, unaware of the way and He guided you, in need and He made you free of need. So don’t crush the orphan, don’t scold the one who asks, and speak of your Lord’s blessing.
points: An orphan, and He gave you shelter
Unaware of the way, and He guided you
In need, and He made you free of need
Don’t drive away the one who asks
sections.matters: The proof that Allah has not left him is his own life story. And the right way to thank Allah for each favour is to show the same care to others.
sections.story: No specific incident. It continues the reply to the taunt by pointing to Allah’s care for the Prophet ﷺ from the very start.
explained: His father died before he was born, and his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, then his uncle Abū Ṭālib, took him in. He did not know the Book or faith, and Allah guided him. He was poor, and Allah made him free of need, through Khadījah’s wealth and a content heart.

So, as you were once an orphan, never be harsh with an orphan. Don’t scold anyone who asks, whether for money or for knowledge: give, or turn him away kindly. And speak of your Lord’s blessings, because talking about them is a way of thanking Him.
teaches: Remember how Allah carried you through your past.
Be gentle and generous with orphans.
Never scold someone who asks for help or knowledge.
Speaking of Allah’s blessings is gratitude.
sections.hook: Three favours (6–8), then three duties (9–11), each opening with ammā. The first two duties are “don’t” (lā taqhar, lā tanhar); the last is a “do”: fa-ḥaddith.

groups.text: By the morning light and the still night, your Lord has not left you or hated you.
What comes later is better for you, and your Lord will give you until you are pleased.
He found you an orphan and sheltered you, unaware and guided you, in need and enriched you.
So don’t crush the orphan, don’t scold the one who asks, and speak of your Lord’s blessing.

1.explain: Wa-ḍ-ḍuḥā: by the morning light, when the sun has risen and its light spreads. Or the whole day, since it is set against the night.

2.explain: By the night when sajā: it covers everything with darkness, settles and grows still.

3.explain: Mā waddaʿaka: your Lord has not left you since He chose you. Wa mā qalā: nor has He hated you since He loved you.
3.why: Revelation paused for some days, and the idolaters said his Lord had abandoned and hated him. Reportedly a woman, said to be Umm Jamīl, taunted, “Your devil has left you,” when he was ill and missed night prayer. Reports differ on why the pause happened.

4.explain: Al-ākhirah, the Hereafter, is better for you than this world. Or: every later stage of your life will be better than the one before. So he lived simply, like a rider resting under a tree.

5.explain: Allah will give you until you are pleased: victory here, and intercession for your ummah there. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Then I won’t be pleased while one of my ummah is in the Fire.”
5.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ was shown the treasures his ummah would be given after him, and it pleased him. Then this ayah was revealed.

6.explain: Did He not find you yatīm, an orphan, and give you shelter? His father died before his birth; his grandfather, then his uncle Abū Ṭālib, raised and protected him.

7.explain: Ḍāll here means unaware, not astray: before prophethood he did not know the Book, the law or faith, and Allah guided him. Another view: lost as a boy in Makkah’s valleys and brought back.

8.explain: ʿĀʾil: in need. Allah made him free of need, through Khadījah’s wealth and later gains, and with a content heart. True wealth is richness of the soul.

9.explain: Fa-lā taqhar: don’t crush the orphan, take his wealth or look down on him. Be like a merciful father to him, since you were an orphan once.

10.explain: Fa-lā tanhar: don’t scold the sāʾil, whether he asks for money or for knowledge. Give what you can, or turn him away gently.

11.explain: Fa-ḥaddith: speak of your Lord’s blessings: prophethood, the Quran and every favour. Talking about them is thanks; hiding them is ingratitude.
